A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Gate and PrivacyPair research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original MiniGPT and LLaVA experiments, ablations, neuron analyses, and human validation of PrivacyPair.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons, appendix analyses, and human validation study.

M1.justification: The feature perturbation procedure, cross-sample neural gate, 0.3 threshold, subject-token gradient truncation, and single-layer and multi-layer editing procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six PrivacyPair categories, English privacy samples from MLLMGuard, and ScienceQA, MME, and POPE evaluations. No training domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the unedited baseline, MEMIT, AlphaEdit, DINM, SKU*, and MemFlex*. The refusal-oriented baseline adaptations and Section 4.5 keyword guardrail comparison also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The models, metrics, 2,640/1,410 PrivacyPair training/test counts, 400 ScienceQA samples, training settings, editing layers, and alpha settings are retained. The added repetition statement discloses reporting practice without establishing a changed evaluation design.

E4.justification: Both retain gate-removal and single-layer/multi-layer ablations, alpha sensitivity, generalization comparisons, success/failure examples, layer-search analysis, and neuron-distribution heatmaps. No new analytical experiment is introduced.

E5.justification: V2 Appendix C.1 newly states that each category of experiments was repeated three times and mean results were reported; v1 Section 8.1 lacks this information. This is newly disclosed repetition information, not evidence of increased runs. No dispersion estimates or confidence intervals are added.

E6.justification: Numerical entries in Tables 1–4 match, as do plotted trends, qualitative examples, and human-validation outcomes. For example, Table 1 retains Neural Gate Safety averages of 0.8918 for MiniGPT and 0.8566 for LLaVA.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the mathematical definitions and objectives remain equivalent, including feature scaling, gate aggregation, and masked gradient updates. No theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about neuron-level editing, PrivacyPair, improved privacy generalization, and preservation of utility.

C2.justification: Section 4.5 adds the speculation that successful generalization to trade secrets may arise from similarities with government-document privacy concepts. The underlying example and existing limitations concerning uneven generalization remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-availability statement and GitHub repository pointer in the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation, hardware, training, and data-construction details otherwise remain the same.

R1.justification: V2 adds Dysca and REVAL citations to the introductory background while retaining the existing research positioning. Consolidation of duplicate MLLMGuard references does not remove a distinct cited work.

P1.justification: V2 adds keywords, corresponding-author information, and acknowledgements, updates affiliation text, and relabels appendix sections A–E. Several specific appendix references become generic references to the Appendix. Most prose and narrative ordering remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The document changes throughout from two columns to a single-column layout, with different margins, typography, running headers, and caption formatting. The same seven figures and four tables are extensively resized and repositioned, including text wrapping around Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The new code pointer and explicit three-repetition mean reporting modestly improve reproducibility documentation and transparency. Scientific evidence remains unchanged. Smaller main displays and less precise appendix references impose some readability and navigation costs, limiting the overall gain.
